run_status_note: run_status=partial. 'complete' requires EVERY requested arm to be complete AND every completed arm to have reproduced its historical record exactly. Arms with an absent checkpoint or an error are named above and were NOT silently skipped; a 'partial' run does not cover them and must not be reported as a full re-evaluation. History comparability: none_exact -- this run's numbers CANNOT be compared to the historical numbers. The within-run corrected-vs-legacy label-text comparison remains valid (both sets scored the same regenerated images); what is lost is any claim about what the ORIGINAL records would have become.
evaluation_role_note: CORRECTIVE RE-EVALUATION OF AN ALREADY-INSPECTED SPLIT. The FINAL split was inspected in FINDING65 and FINDING66 before this run; these numbers are DEVELOPMENT measurements that repair a scoring defect (D-013). They are NOT a fresh held-out confirmation and must not be reported as one.
method_note: The original images were never saved, so the original pixels cannot be re-scored. Images are REGENERATED from the recorded prompts and seeds and then scored under both label-text sets. Matching seeds are a reason to EXPECT similar images, not proof: determinism is an assumption, tested per arm by determinism_probe against the historical records, and NOT presumed to hold.

label_mismatch.interpretation: The evaluator used inconsistent label text. The effect on scores and conclusions is unresolved pending corrected evaluation. Direction and magnitude are NOT established by the existence of the mismatch; an underscore-vs-space edit changes the token sequence and so the text embedding, but the sign of the resulting similarity change is empirical.

exposure_in_historical_records.framing: Small margins mean the outcomes are sensitive to label text; they do not indicate which way. This count is NOT a bound on how many decisions could move: the decision is a closed-set argmax over all twelve labels, so an image predicted as an UNCHANGED label (church, parachute, tench) can also flip when a competitor's text changes. Images predicted on a differing label are where a change is most directly visible, not where it is confined.

unmodified_baseline.scope_note: Byte-identity is proven only from baseline_taken_at onward. For the period before that date the evidence is mtime only, and no stronger claim is made: the prior hash record (outputs/provenance_manifest.json) predates this repair and truncates its per-file hashes to 16 hex characters.

numerics.decision: closed-set argmax over the label axis; NO reject option, NO threshold

paired_scoring.design: Both label-text sets are scored on ONE image-feature tensor per image, so the image side is bit-identical across the pair and any difference in the decision is attributable to the label text alone.

sets.corrected: gen_eval.LABELS (the text every H number uses)
sets.legacy: gen_eval.LAB_KEY (the text the pre-repair FINAL records used)

paired_scoring.identity_mapping: gen_eval.LAB_KEY, identical under both sets, so prediction indices mean the same concept either way

code.git_note: no git repository at the source tree root; code identity is the per-file sha256 below

provenance.environment_caveat: These are THIS run's versions. The original FINAL run recorded none, so no claim that the two environments match is possible. This is the main reason bit-identical regeneration cannot be asserted from matching seeds.

models.variant_note: variant='fp16' is passed to from_pretrained for every arm, matching gen_eval_final.py. An arm whose repo has no such variant will FAIL loudly and be recorded as failed, not silently fall back.

classifier.revision_note: UNPINNED upstream in every historical run; left unpinned here so the re-scoring uses the same locally cached weights rather than silently introducing a second classifier identity into the comparison.

numerics.decision: closed-set argmax over the label axis; NO reject option, NO threshold

inference.scheduler: recorded PER ARM from the instantiated pipeline (see arm record 'scheduler'); gen_eval_final.py used the repo default, not an override
